SMTO-SKL-0026 — This calendar event changed since SMTO last read it

GUID: dc0fbbe1-9726-5620-b279-ad6a7113414d
Slug: google-calendar-precondition-failed
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: google-calendar

What happened

  • Someone or something changed this event after SMTO looked at it, so SMTO stopped instead of overwriting their changes. Your edit wasn't applied.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the event in Google Calendar and see what's different, such as a new time, title or guest list. Another person, device or app updated the event after SMTO read it.
  2. Ask SMTO to read the event again so it sees the latest version. SMTO only changes an event when it's working from its newest version.
  3. Decide whether your change still makes sense with the new details, then ask SMTO to make it again. This keeps your change from silently undoing someone else's update.

What success looks like

  • Your change appears in Google Calendar and the other person's updates are still there.

If it still fails

  • If the event keeps changing, agree with the other organizer or guests on who edits it, then try again. Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO if it still fails.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Calendar write was refused because the event's current ETag no longer matches the expected ETag (pre-write read mismatch, or Google returned 412 Precondition Failed).

What this means

  • Google returns HTTP 412, or the current event ETag differs from the supplied expected ETag before writing. This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Google returns HTTP 412, or the current event ETag differs from the supplied expected ETag before writing.

How to diagnose it

  • Read the exact event and compare current ETag and desired changes.

How to fix it

  • Read the exact calendar_id and event_id again (google_calendar.event) to get its current state and ETag, review what changed, and issue a new change with the new ETag only after resolving the conflict. The same applies to calendar and calendar-list changes.
  • Read the exact event again, review the current state and ETag, and request a new edit only after resolving the conflicting changes.

Retry and execution caution

  • Read the exact event again, review the current state and ETag, and request a new edit only after resolving the conflicting changes.

How to verify the fix

  • A deliberate new edit uses the observed current version after conflicts are reconciled.

What not to do

  • Do not expose credentials or private Calendar content in diagnostics.
  • Do not blindly repeat writes after uncertain provider effects.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
